chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man and a woman; her husband had sodomized her son (who was from another father) and had penetrated him, and the witnesses testified to that. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ordered that he be struck with the sword until he died, and the boy was struck with less than the Hadd (fixed penalty), and he said: 'But, had you been mature, I would have killed you because you had made it possible for him to penetrate you through your penetration.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sodomy between a father and his son in Shia jurisprudence according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the application of Hadd for sodomy (Liwat) by Imam Ali (AS), distinguishing between the active and passive parties based on maturity and consent. The father was executed by the sword, while the boy received Ta'zir (discretionary punishment) rather than the full Hadd, with the Imam noting that if the boy had been mature, he too would have been killed for allowing the penetration.
